償 concerns making up for a loss, recompensing someone or making amends. 補償 ほしょう is compensation for loss; 償う つぐなう can describe compensating for a loss or atoning for wrongdoing. Not every use implies that someone committed a crime.

The visible parts are 亻, the side form of 人, and 賞 on the right. Modern-shape mnemonic: picture a person handing over something valuable to make good a loss. This is a visual memory aid, not a historical or phonetic explanation.
補償 ほしょう — compensation for loss
償う つぐなう — make amends; compensate for loss
In 償う, the kanji represents つぐな and う is okurigana. Both sourced readings are retained and selected for reading questions.
補償 ほしょう — compensation for loss
償う つぐなう — make amends; compensate for loss
賞 also has ショウ, but its prize or reward meaning does not make 賞 and 償 interchangeable. Notice the extra 亻 in 償.
補, "supplement; make good," overlaps in supplying what is missing. Learn the whole word rather than dividing compensation and supplementation into absolute categories.
儀, "ceremony; formal conduct," 僧, "Buddhist monk; priest," and 億, "hundred million," share 亻 but have different right-hand shapes.

償う is a transitive godan verb: make up for a loss or debt, or make amends for wrongdoing. The loss, debt or wrongdoing being made up for takes を. Compensation can involve money or goods; making amends can also involve actions.
彼は損害を償いました。 (かれはそんがいをつぐないました。) - He compensated for the damage.
彼は自分の過ちを償おうとしています。 (かれはじぶんのあやまちをつぐなおうとしています。) - He is trying to make amends for his mistake.
Forms include 償います (つぐないます), 償わない (つぐなわない), 償った (つぐなった), and 償って (つぐなって).
償 contributes making good a loss or making amends. つぐな is represented by the kanji; う is okurigana. The compound reading ショウ does not replace つぐな in this verb.

補償 (ほしょう), used with する, focuses on compensation for loss. 補う (おぎなう) is broader supplementation or making up for a shortage; the words can overlap in loss contexts. Apologizing is not necessarily the same as making amends, and there is no single opposite that reverses both the compensation and atonement senses.

償う does not always imply moral guilt: 損害 (そんがい), damage or loss, can be its object. Conversely, making amends for a mistake need not mean simply paying money. Context determines what would count as making good the harm.
The dictionary also records 償う as つぐのう. Nikkoku identifies つぐなう as the form much used today; this article teaches つぐなう rather than treating every recorded pronunciation as the modern default.
Dictionary: JMdict, entry 1346020. Usage and alternate reading: Daijisen and Nikkoku, 償う.
補償 is compensation that makes good a loss. It is a noun and forms a transitive verb with する. With 補償する, the loss being compensated for takes を.
会社は事故による損害を補償しました。 (かいしゃはじこによるそんがいをほしょうしました。) - The company compensated for the damage caused by the accident.
私たちは補償を求めています。 (わたしたちはほしょうをもとめています。) - We are seeking compensation.
In the second example, 補償 is the noun object of 求める (もとめる), "seek." Seeking compensation does not mean that it has already been paid.
補 contributes supplying what is missing; 償 contributes recompense or making good a loss. The near-synonymous parts reinforce the idea of making up for a loss. 補 supplies ホ and 償 supplies ショウ in ほしょう.

償う (つぐなう) can mean compensating for a loss or making amends. 補う (おぎなう) is broader: it can also mean supplementing an explanation. 保証 (ほしょう), "guarantee; warranty," is a different word despite the shared pronunciation. A promise or warranty is not itself compensation paid for a loss. There is no single everyday antonym covering every compensation context.

This article focuses on practical compensation for loss, not the separate psychological or technical uses. Legal sources can distinguish particular types of 補償 from damages, but ordinary use can be broader; do not infer that 補償 always excludes damages or automatically establishes someone's liability. Whether compensation is owed or paid depends on the actual circumstances and conditions.

補 concerns supplying what is missing, supplementing or making good a shortage. 候補 こうほ names a candidate, while 補う おぎなう directly expresses supplementing or compensating.

Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology: Imagine a new patch, the right-hand 甫-shaped block, supplying a missing part of a garment 衤. This is a mnemonic rather than a claim about the component's historical role.
The indexing radical 衣 appears as left-hand 衤, not the similar-looking 礻.
候補 こうほ - candidate; possible choice
補う おぎなう - supplement; make up for
候補 こうほ - candidate; possible choice
補う おぎなう - supplement; make up for
補償 ほしょう - compensation for loss
補充 ほじゅう - replenishment; refilling
Compare 捕, capture: its left-hand 扌 differs from the clothing form 衤 in 補.
補う is a transitive godan verb, not an adjective meaning enough. Learn 候補 as a whole word rather than expecting the two character glosses to reproduce every modern use.

補う means supplying something missing, making up a shortage or loss, or supplementing something insufficient. It is a transitive godan verb. The shortage, lack, or material being supplemented takes を.
足りない生活費をアルバイトで補っています。 (たりないせいかつひをアルバイトでおぎなっています。) - I make up the shortfall in living expenses with a part-time job.
図を使って説明を補いました。 (ずをつかってせつめいをおぎないました。) - I supplemented the explanation with a diagram.
Forms include 補います (おぎないます), 補わない (おぎなわない), 補った (おぎなった), and 補って (おぎなって).
補 contributes supplying what is missing. おぎな is represented by the kanji and う is okurigana. The compound reading ホ does not replace おぎな in this verb.

埋める (うめる) also covers filling a gap or making up a loss. 足す (たす) and 加える (くわえる) describe adding; 補う makes the insufficiency or missing part important. 補充 (ほじゅう) is replenishment; 補足 (ほそく) is supplementation.

The supplement need not be money or a physical patch. The diagram example adds information that the explanation lacks. English "compensate" here does not automatically mean paying legal damages: 補償する (ほしょうする) is the relevant comparison for compensation or reparation.
